plainTranslation: A's dreams meets B's feelings. The opposition pulls them into push-and-pull.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryDeep: Their idealism, vagueness, and dreams press against your feelings, needs, and sense of safety. It catches often enough that you both feel it, and it keeps asking to be worked out. Name it directly instead of letting it build in silence.
tension: But oppositions invite projection. One person may begin filling in the blanks with what they hope is true. The Moon person may assume the Neptune person feels the same depth, needs the same closeness, or understands the relationship in the same way. The Neptune person may drift in and out of emotional availability, not always realizing how much meaning the Moon person has placed on the connection. When reality arrives, the disappointment can be painful. You may realize you were not only relating to the person in front of you, but also to the feeling they awakened in you. The longing was real. The care may have been real. But the story built around it may not have been.
advice: The invitation here is to keep returning to what is actually happening. Notice where you are hoping, assuming, rescuing, or waiting for the other person to become clearer than they are willing to be. This connection can be beautiful when care and clarity are allowed to exist together. It hurts most when the dream of being understood becomes more important than the truth of who is actually there.
summaryShort: Their idealism, vagueness, and dreams press against your feelings, needs, and sense of safety.
